Week 6: Usability Testing

Planning, running, and analyzing small studies

CMSC 434 · Fall 2026 · October 9, 2026

Why test with users?

  • •Designers are not typical users
  • •Five participants find most major problems
  • •Testing early is cheaper than fixing late
  • •Watch what people do, not what they say
  • •Iterate: test, fix, and test again

Think-aloud protocol

In a think-aloud session, the participant narrates their thoughts while completing realistic tasks. The facilitator stays neutral, avoids leading questions, and only prompts with short phrases such as "What are you thinking now?" Sessions are usually recorded with screen capture and audio, so the team can review hesitations, errors, and workarounds later. Concurrent think-aloud can slow participants down, so task times collected this way should not be compared directly with silent sessions. Retrospective think-aloud avoids this cost but relies on memory, which is less reliable after long tasks.

Running a session

  • 1.Welcome the participant and get consent
  • 2.Explain the think-aloud method
  • 3.Give one task at a time:
  • a)Read the task aloud
  • b)Start the timer
  • c)Note errors and hesitations
  • 4.Finish with a short questionnaire
  • 5.Thank and compensate the participant

Logging task events (Swift)

struct TaskEvent: Codable {
    let id: UUID
    let name: String
    let startedAt: Date
    var errors = 0
}

func log(_ e: TaskEvent) {
    print("[\(e.name)] errors=\(e.errors)")
}

Measuring efficiency

Mean task time: 74.2 s (SD = 18.6 s)

Error rate = errors / attempts = 12 / 40 = 30%

SUS score: 68 is about average; 80.3 or higher is excellent

Completion target: ≥ 90% within 2 min

p < 0.05 with n = 12 per group

Reporting findings

  • •Lead with the three most severe problems
  • •Show a short clip for each problem
  • •Pair every problem with a concrete fix
  • •Keep the full list in an appendix

Source: adapted from course notes, Week 6. Severity uses a 0-4 scale.

Severity ratings

0: Not a usability problem

1: Cosmetic, fix if time allows

2: Minor, low priority

3: Major, high priority

4: Catastrophe, must fix before release
